text:
maya: just pushed delta-embed (int6 6-bit per-tensor) to the staging bucket and wired it into the eval job. quick summary: recall@10 down ~1.8% vs fp16 on our semantic bench, silhouette dropped slightly, but latency and throughput look solid. can someone eyeball the cluster plots?

jorge: on it — can you paste the eval job id?

maya: job id `run_eval_2026_03_20_07` (staging), config: `--quant=int6 --per_tensor=true --seed=42 --k=10`

sara: pulling logs now. initial numbers:
```
model    recall@1  recall@5  recall@10  silhouette  qps
fp16     0.472     0.742     0.812      0.34        18.2
int6     0.461     0.728     0.794      0.31        27.5
delta    0.459     0.725     0.794      0.30        28.0
```

alex: thanks — rough drop at R@10 ~0.018 absolute (1.8%). silhouette down 0.04 which is small but worth investigating. any per-language splits?

sara: yeah english drop biggest: R@10 -2.3% abs, multilang low-resource actually stable (tiny up). weird. attaching UMAP images in the staging artifact link: https://staging-artifacts/redwood/delta-embed/run_eval_2026_03_20_07/plots

maya: I noticed mean vector norms are a bit lower after int6 quant: mean_norm fp16=7.9, int6=6.8. could be contributing to kNN threshold mismatch.

jorge: try re-normalizing before indexing (L2) and rerun recall calc, that isolates whether magnitude shift is the culprit. also run a small kmeans silhouette on 50k samples to verify cluster structure.

alex: repro command I'm going to run locally: `python eval/recalc_recall.py --data subset50k --model delta-int6 --normalize --k 10`. I'll post results in ~10m.

ci-bot: smoke tests finished for run_eval_2026_03_20_07 — status: SUCCESS. artifacts: /artifacts/run_eval_2026_03_20_07 (17 files) :white_check_mark:

alex: quick rerun with L2 normalize:
```
int6 (normalized) recall@10 = 0.806 (vs fp16 0.812)
silhouette = 0.33
```

maya: okay that recovered ~60% of the gap at R@10. so magnitude was a big part. still want to dig into per-layer quant impact (early vs late attention).

sara: agree. can we also run a fallback routing sim in the serving harness (route to fp16 for low-confidence queries) and measure user-visible hit rate? want to see operational risk.

maya: good idea. I'll open a tiny canary: 1% traffic, fallback when knn score < 0.45. will post numbers after tonight's run.

jorge: suggested next steps: (1) per-layer quant experiments (int6 only last 6 layers), (2) eval w/ faiss HNSW parameters tuned (efSearch up) — sometimes recall hits are recoverable with index tweaks, (3) run high-recall subset of user queries to estimate impact on product metrics.

alex: logging a ticket for per-layer quant experiments and routing sim: RED-ML-1287. assigning maya + jorge.

maya: thanks — if we can get per-layer gradient-free quant analysis by EOD that'd be ideal. otherwise we'll consider rolling int6 to dedicated canary with normalize pre-index as interim. :thumbsup:

sara: noted — saving plots and eval tables to the canonical audit: https://redwood-internal/evals/delta-int6-audit
